title: Database blip empties the pool
description: Each checkout server's /healthz endpoint queries the primary database and returns 503 if the query fails. During a 15-second database failover, the load balancer marks every checkout server unhealthy and returns 503 to all users for over a minute, even after the database recovers. Which change best prevents this?

options.text: Lower the health check interval to 200 ms so servers are marked healthy again faster.
options.explanation: Faster checks add probe load and still eject the entire pool during the dependency outage; they do not fix what the check measures.

options.text: Switch the pool from round robin to least connections.
options.explanation: The balancing algorithm only chooses among healthy endpoints; with all of them ejected, it has nothing to choose from.

options.text: Make /healthz report only whether the process can serve, rely on passive outlier detection for real errors, and set a panic threshold so a mostly-unhealthy pool still receives traffic.
options.explanation: Shallow health checks stop a shared dependency from ejecting every server at once, outlier detection still removes individually broken servers, and the panic threshold treats 'everything is unhealthy' as a bad signal rather than a reason to serve nothing.

options.text: Add a second health check that pings the database from the load balancer itself.
options.explanation: This couples the load balancer even more tightly to the database and repeats the same failure mode.
